articles.title: NatureLens — An AI That Tells You to Touch Grass.
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge — Week 1: Touch Grass What if your phone could help you notice the world instead of distracting you from it? We spend hours looking…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge — Week 1: Touch Grass What if your phone could help you notice the world instead of distracting you from it? We spend hours looking at screens to discover things that are literally sitting outside our windows. A bird on a branch. A strange leaf. A mushroom beside a trail. A flower you've walked past a hundred times. So I built NatureLens — a local-AI-powered outdoor field guide designed around one simple idea: Touch grass. Notice more. Instead of asking people to search the internet every time they see something interesting, NatureLens turns their phone into an interactive field guide . Point your camera at something. Observe it. Let local AI help you understand it. Then go outside and look again.
articles.author: Ranit Das

articles.title: How to Actually Fix Roblox FPS Drops on PC
articles.excerpt: You're having a great run in Roblox. The frame rate is smooth, everything is clicking, and then it happens: you walk into a crowded hub, turn the camera, or trigger a few particle effects, and suddenl…
articles.body: You're having a great run in Roblox. The frame rate is smooth, everything is clicking, and then it happens: you walk into a crowded hub, turn the camera, or trigger a few particle effects, and suddenly your game turns into a slideshow. It's incredibly frustrating. But before you start randomly toggling every graphics setting in sight or blaming your hardware, take a breath. "Low FPS" doesn't automatically mean your PC is obsolete. Roblox is a unique engine, and performance can be bottlenecked by your CPU, GPU, RAM, thermals, background apps, or even just how a specific game developer coded their map. Let's figure out what's actually happening so you can fix it properly. Step 1: Diagnose, Don't Guess Not all "lag" is created equal.
articles.author: Tzukizy

articles.title: The Origins of the Boolean
articles.excerpt: Data types are fundamental concepts in modern programming languages. True and False. The Mathematical Analysis of Logic (1847) and An Investigation of the Laws of Thought (1854). The Beginnings: 1930…
articles.body: Data types are fundamental concepts in modern programming languages. When you begin learning them, the first type you encounter is the Boolean, represented by two possible outcomes: True and False . However, the most curious aspect of this type is its name; translating it into your language yields the word for logic—yet one might wonder, where exactly does the logic come in? A bit of research reveals that the person who first transformed logic into something measurable, actionable, and usable was the mathematician George Boole. He laid the foundations of Boolean algebra through two seminal works: The Mathematical Analysis of Logic (1847) and An Investigation of the Laws of Thought (1854).
articles.author: Mh. Saleem Al-Zayat

articles.title: Your holiday library is probably right. Here are the days it got wrong for us, and the correction layer we built
articles.excerpt: If you calculate business days, delivery dates or payroll in more than one country, you probably use the excellent open-source holidays package for Python. We do too. It covers more than 200 countries…
articles.body: If you calculate business days, delivery dates or payroll in more than one country, you probably use the excellent open-source holidays package for Python. We do too. It covers more than 200 countries and territories and is right almost all of the time. "Almost" matters when you publish holiday lists that people plan around. So before we list a country, we compare the library's dates with the government's own announcements. Thirteen countries needed at least one correction. None of these are really bugs. Governments publish decisions the library can't know in advance. But the patterns are worth knowing if holiday data feeds anything important. The five kinds of mismatch we found 1. Holidays moved by decree to make a long weekend.

articles.title: Comparing Transactional Email API Providers for Startup Welcome Emails Beyond SMTP Relays
articles.excerpt: Short answer: for a customer-support system that must send a compliance notice and later prove what happened, choose an API-first email service when application code owns the workflow. Choose an SMTP-…
articles.body: Short answer: for a customer-support system that must send a compliance notice and later prove what happened, choose an API-first email service when application code owns the workflow. Choose an SMTP-capable provider when a CMS, ticketing tool, or legacy mail library owns it. The decisive artifact is not the welcome message itself. It is a durable record connecting the triggering account data, the exact notice document, the send request, and the delivery events. SendGrid, Amazon SES, Postmark, and Resend can all be reasonable choices, but their integration surfaces shape how much evidence-building code your team must own. Infrai is another API-first option when a small team also wants account usage, PDF generation, and email behind one REST contract.

articles.title: Migrating a Large Table Without Locking Production
articles.excerpt: GoCardless once took around 15 seconds of unexpected API downtime from a planned migration. The tables being changed were empty. The statement was fast. It didn't matter, because the migration needed…
articles.body: GoCardless once took around 15 seconds of unexpected API downtime from a planned migration. The tables being changed were empty. The statement was fast. It didn't matter, because the migration needed a lock on a heavily used parent table, a long-running read was already holding a conflicting lock, and every API query that arrived after that queued up behind the migration until clients timed out. They wrote it up in Zero-downtime Postgres migrations: the hard parts . That story is the best correction I know to the way this topic usually gets framed. "Tables too big to lock" suggests the danger is size: a billion rows, a rewrite that takes forty minutes. Size is a real problem, but it's the second one.

articles.title: Computing Eid, Rosh Hashanah and Lunar New Year dates in JavaScript with Intl calendars, and where it goes wrong
articles.excerpt: Most "how many days until…" code is easy until someone asks about Eid al-Fitr, Hanukkah or Lunar New Year. These holidays follow lunar or lunisolar calendars, so they move against the Gregorian calend…
articles.body: Most "how many days until…" code is easy until someone asks about Eid al-Fitr, Hanukkah or Lunar New Year. These holidays follow lunar or lunisolar calendars, so they move against the Gregorian calendar every year. You don't need a library for most of them. Modern JavaScript engines ship ICU, and Intl.DateTimeFormat can render any date in the Hebrew, Islamic (Umm al-Qura) or Chinese calendar. With a little scanning, that gives you the Gregorian date of a holiday. It also has a few traps. Below is the approach we use, plus the three places it went wrong for us. The idea: scan the year and ask Intl what day it is Intl converts from Gregorian to another calendar, but there's no built-in conversion back.
